problem: Erdos #126: f(n)/log n -> infinity, equivalently g(k) = exp(o(k)) where g(k) is the max size of a set of distinct positive integers whose off-diagonal pairwise sums are all S-smooth for a set S of k primes
headline: The 1934 Erdos-Turan bound g(k) <= 3*2^(k-1)-1 is still the record; the S-unit route (Gyory-Stewart-Tijdeman 1986) is quantitatively worse (49^k) but isolates the single lever, and a subexponential uniform bound on the number of solutions of the two-variable S-unit equation implies Erdos #126.
search_scope: erdosproblems.com/126 bibliography; Erdos-Turan 1934 full text; Gyory-Stewart-Tijdeman I full text incl. proofs; forward citation chase to Feb 2026; S-unit counting literature; OEIS. Targeted, not exhaustive.

theorems.statement: The two-term sums of 3*2^(k-1) positive integers cannot all be composed of k given primes.
theorems.helps: incumbent record; only bound of the right shape

theorems.statement: 'The order of the maximum n(k) ... is probably n(k)=O(k^{1+eps})'
theorems.helps: shows #126 is far weaker than what the authors expected

theorems.cite: Erdos & Suranyi, Topics in the Theory of Numbers, Springer 2003
Gyory, Stewart & Tijdeman, Compositio Math. 59 (1986), 81-88, Thm 1
theorems.statement: A,B finite positive, |B|>=2, k=|A|: omega(prod_{a,b}(a+b)) > c*log k
theorems.verification: primary, full text incl. section 3 proof
theorems.helps: structurally yes (isolates the bottleneck), numerically no (worse than 2^k)

theorems.statement: lambda x + mu y = nu z has at most 3*7^(2w+3) coprime triples composed of w given primes
theorems.verification: primary as quoted in T3; original not read
theorems.helps: THE lever: exp(o(k)) here implies Erdos #126

theorems.statement: for all eps>0 and large k there are A,B with |A|=k, |B|=2 and omega(prod(a+b)) < (1/8+eps)(log k)^2 loglog k
theorems.helps: yes as a map: blocks polynomial bounds on the two-set route, leaves the whole subexponential range open

theorems.statement: x+y=1 in a rank-r group has at most 2^(8r+8) solutions; weighted version 2^(9(r+1))

theorems.cite: Evertse, Schlickewei & Schmidt, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002)
theorems.statement: a_1x_1+...+a_nx_n=1 has at most e^{(6n)^{3n}(r+1)} non-degenerate solutions
theorems.helps: no; needed only by the strictly worse 4-element route

theorems.cite: Sarkozy & Stewart; Balog & Sarkozy (as cited in T3 sec.1)
theorems.statement: dense A,B in [1,N] force P(a+b) >> N
theorems.helps: no: extremal sets here are extremely sparse

theorems.statement: Erdos-Turan analogue over Eulerian integers, omega_E > (log(|A|-1)-log 18)/log 2
theorems.helps: no; corroborates that no improvement of T1/T3 exists as of Feb 2026

theorems.cite: derived here; equals the trivial f(n) << n/log n on erdosproblems.com/126
theorems.statement: A={1,...,m} has all sums < 2m, so k = pi(2m-1)
theorems.helps: gives the only nontrivial lower bound on g(k) found anywhere

definitions.g(k): max |A| with all off-diagonal a+b S-smooth
definitions.g_2(k): max |A| such that there exist b1 != b2 with a+b1 and a+b2 S-smooth for all a in A
definitions.N(k): max over nonzero lambda,mu,nu of the number of coprime triples (x,y,z) composed of k given primes with lambda x + mu y = nu z

steps.proof: pick b1,b2 in an extremal A and apply the definition to A minus {b1,b2}
GST 1986 sec.3 verbatim: a_i gives (x,y,z) = (a_i+b1, a_i+b2, 1) solving x - y = (b1-b2) z; z=1 makes the triple coprime; distinct a_i give distinct triples

steps.claim: log N(k) = o(k) implies g(k) = exp(o(k)) implies Erdos #126

derived_reduction.converse: FALSE / not available. #126 does not imply the S-unit improvement: step 2 discards all but 2(n-2) of the binom(n,2) sums, and the loss is real -- g_2(k) >= exp(c sqrt(k/log k)) by T5 while g(k) <= 3*2^(k-1) by T1.
derived_reduction.room: exp((4+o(1)) sqrt(k/log k)) <= g_2(k) <= 3*7^(2k+3). Everything strictly below exp(o(k)) in that window settles #126, and no known construction obstructs it.

closest_theorem_that_would_imply_subexpo.statement: A uniform bound N(k) <= exp(o(k)) on the number of coprime S-unit solutions of lambda x + mu y = nu z, |S| = k, uniform in the coefficients and in the choice of primes.
closest_theorem_that_would_imply_subexpo.status: open problem in Diophantine approximation; I did not find an explicit conjecture that the subexponential bound is true

audit_of_r_186989.finding: Arm 2's parity headline (2 in S is decisive) is stated verbatim on page 1 of Erdos-Turan 1934

Arm 3's kill is stronger than claimed: supermultiplicativity gives g(k) >= 2^k, which must fit inside T1's 3*2^(k-1)-1, forcing the 1934 bound to be sharp up to a factor 3/2 and contradicting the 1934 authors' own conjecture n(k)=O(k^{1+eps})
The measured table 2,4,5,6,8,10,11 carries no asymptotic information the literature lacks; the trivial construction A={1..m} already gives g(k) >> k log k
audit_of_r_186989.effect: confirms the hunt's own 'seven points decide nothing' verdict

not_settled: Whether log N(k) = o(k) is a stated conjecture of the field. Costs one look at Evertse-Gyory, Unit Equations in Diophantine Number Theory (CUP 2015), ch. 6.
Whether max(A) is effectively bounded in terms of S. The obvious Baker/Gyory-Yu route is circular because the coefficient nu = b1-b2 is bounded only by max(A).
T2 (2^k+1) and T5 (constant 1/8) are secondary citations via Furedi-Gyarmati 2026 and were not checked against the originals.
